definitions.explanation: The act of warning or disciplining oneself to avoid repeating mistakes or falling into bad habits. Reflects a deliberate effort at self-correction.

examples.japanese: {自戒|じかい}を{込|こ}めて{言|い}う。
examples.english: I say this as a warning to myself as well.

examples.japanese: {同|おな}じ{失敗|しっぱい}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}さないよう{自戒|じかい}した。
examples.english: I warned myself not to repeat the same mistake.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はあの{経験|けいけん}を{自戒|じかい}の{念|ねん}として{心|こころ}に{刻|きざ}んでいる。
examples.english: He keeps that experience engraved in his heart as a reminder to himself.

notes:
A compound of {自|じ} (self) and {戒|かい} (admonition, warning). Can be used as a noun or as a suru verb ({自戒|じかい}する).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自戒|じかい}を{込|こ}めて (with self-admonition; including a warning to oneself)
- {自戒|じかい}の{念|ねん} (a sense of self-admonition)
- {自戒|じかい}する (to admonish oneself)

The phrase {自戒|じかい}を{込|こ}めて is commonly used when someone criticizes a behavior while acknowledging they are also guilty of it — similar to saying "speaking from my own experience" or "I need to hear this too." Note the homophone {次回|じかい} (next time), which is a completely different word.
